step_goal: Define one minimal but complete intake contract that gives HSConfig enough identity, scope, provenance, and mode information to generate deck-specific preview artifacts without hard-coding deck templates or making runtime claims.

required_inputs.name: deck_name
required_inputs.purpose: Human-readable label for output folders, reports, and operator context.
required_inputs.governance: Use for labeling only; never use deck_name to infer hero, cards, format, or strategy.

required_inputs.name: deck_code
required_inputs.governance: Decode first, then derive hero, format, card counts, sideboards, and deck fingerprint from the decoded payload rather than from remembered archetype labels.

required_inputs.name: format
required_inputs.purpose: Optional caller-supplied format hint or override.
required_inputs.governance: If absent, derive from the decoded deckstring. If present, normalize and compare against the decoded value so mismatches become explicit blockers or degraded status instead of silent assumptions.

required_inputs.name: runtime_root
required_inputs.purpose: Target HearthRanger runtime root for packaging, fake write planning, guarded apply planning, and later drift checks.
required_inputs.governance: Carry this path in the contract even when the current step is preview-only. The presence of runtime_root does not authorize writes.

required_inputs.name: target_config_mode
required_inputs.purpose: Declare whether the caller wants preview-only authoring or a later runtime-targeted package lineage.
required_inputs.governance: Normalize to an explicit enum such as preview, fake_write_package, or guarded_apply_candidate. Step 01 may plan for later apply lineage but must remain read-only.

required_inputs.name: card_data_source
required_inputs.purpose: Explicit card-data source used to resolve DBF ids into CardIDs and card metadata.
required_inputs.governance: Require an explicit path or pinned source reference. Do not resolve card identity from deck_name, class nickname, or guide pages when explicit card data is available.

required_inputs.name: source_citation_bundle
required_inputs.purpose: Initial provenance registry for deckstring facts, card-data facts, and later guide or meta claims.
required_inputs.governance: Every non-trivial claim must carry source id, provider, URL or file path, claim layer, capture time or pinned-local status, content hash when practical, confidence, freshness rule, and trust ceiling.

produced_outputs.purpose: Canonical Step 01 record containing deck_name, deck_code, normalized format, runtime_root, target_config_mode, deck slug, deck fingerprint, source refs, and read-only scope flags.
Decoded deck artifact with hero, cards, sideboards, identity diagnostics, unknown DBF ids, and source refs for deckstring and card-data resolution.
Seeded source registry that starts with stable identity facts and can later absorb dated guide_interpretation and dated_meta_claim rows without losing provenance.
Read-only readiness record for local roots, planned artifacts, missing inputs, and blocked or degraded reasons.

reliable_uses: Prove deck identity from deck_code plus explicit card-data provenance.
Derive or normalize format before any guide lookup or config authoring.
Bind every later Step 1 artifact to one deck fingerprint so deck swaps and stale evidence are detectable.
Carry runtime_root and target_config_mode as packaging scope metadata without implying runtime mutation.
Seed a provenance model that distinguishes stable_reference_fact, deck_identity_fact, guide_interpretation, and dated_meta_claim.
Authorize aggressive preview authoring only on documented config surfaces and only when the claim stays source-backed and syntax-compatible.
limitations: This step cannot prove CONFIG_LOAD_OK, RUNTIME_SAMPLED, gameplay improvement, finetune readiness, or patch correctness.
This step must not infer card identity, hero identity, or strategy from deck_name alone.
This step must not let guide prose or current meta pages become runtime proof or guarded-apply authority.
This step cannot decide undocumented VisionAI behavior, hidden-information logic, or owner-sensitive conditionals as auto-generated runtime rows.
This step cannot authorize GlobalValues retuning or post-run patch promotion without fresh runtime evidence.
This step should treat symbolic combo plans, conditional mulligan prose, and broad matchup narratives as upstream intent unless they can be reduced to documented preview-safe surfaces.

relevant_config_surfaces.step01_role: Potential preview target once guide-backed mulligan intent is compiled into documented keep or discard rows.
Potential preview target for card-local behavior rows once per-card intent is source-backed and syntax-safe.
Potential preview target only as a baseline-aware contract surface; Step 01 should not treat broad tuning claims as proven.
Potential preview target only when sequencing is concrete, documented, and reducible to card-id-level rows.
Packaging surface for mapping the generated deck slug to the runtime package directory.

aggressive_generation_policy.principle: Be aggressive about preserving deck-specific guide intent, but conservative about what becomes runtime-shaped JSON.
rules: Anchor identity to deck_code, decoded cards, and explicit card data first.
Use deck-neutral compilers that operate on card ids, role tags, patch surfaces, and source refs rather than on hard-coded deck names or archetype templates.
Allow guide-backed claims to enrich archetype summary, mulligan anchors, card roles, usage expectations, board-value intent, and config-surface intent before games are played.
Emit preview candidates only on documented surfaces and only when the claim survives syntax validation and provenance checks.
Preserve unsupported or symbolic intent as suppressed rows, review notes, explicit low-confidence records, or contract gaps instead of silently dropping it.
Keep preview mode first. A request for later apply lineage may change packaging metadata, but not Step 01 authority.

validation_gates: Explicit card-data input must exist and resolve deck DBF ids as far as possible; unknown DBF ids must remain visible.
decklist_fingerprint, deck_code_hash, unresolved_card_count, and card_count_total must be materialized.
Normalized format must be present, either decoded from deckstring or validated against an explicit caller value.
runtime_root must be recorded and classified as scope metadata, not as write authority.
target_config_mode must be normalized to an allowed enum and must not bypass preview-first workflow boundaries.
source_evidence_index must contain at least the deckstring decode fact and the card-data source fact.
All generated Step 01 artifacts must remain read-only with runtime_write_performed=false or equivalent scope metadata.
Any later guide-derived claim must carry freshness and trust-ceiling metadata before downstream steps can treat it as more than a generic fallback.
architectural_implications: HSConfig should expose a dedicated intake layer that is separate from research interpretation and separate from config authoring.
The intake contract should own deck identity normalization, deck fingerprinting, format normalization, runtime_root capture, target_config_mode normalization, and source-registry seeding.
The research layer should consume the input-scope contract and source_evidence_index rather than raw deck_name strings or ad hoc notes.
The config-authoring layer should accept only documented preview-safe intent maps plus explicit mode metadata, and should never read guide pages directly.
HSConfig should keep a preview-first state machine: intake -> research contract -> gameplan or intent maps -> config preview -> fake package -> guarded apply later.
Any CLI or API surface should make the deck-neutral boundary explicit by requiring deck_code and explicit card data, while treating deck_name as a label.

recommended_contracts.purpose: Minimal Step 01 contract for deck identity, scope, mode, and provenance seeds.
Decoded deck artifact with hero, cards, sideboards, unknown ids, and identity diagnostics.
Read-only local-roots and planned-artifacts readiness check.
Typed source registry for stable facts, guide interpretations, and dated meta claims.
Source-backed per-card semantics contract built only after Step 01 has established clean identity and provenance anchors.

never_autogenerate_without: Explicit card-data provenance sufficient to resolve card ids or to make unresolved ids explicit.
A materialized deck fingerprint and deck_code_hash.
A recorded runtime_root for any runtime-targeted package lineage.
At least one stable identity source and one card-data source recorded in source_evidence_index.
Clear separation between source-backed preview intent and runtime proof boundaries.

must_cite_sources.reason: Primary local evidence for required intake fields, deck-neutral card-data requirement, fingerprinting, format capture, and source_refs shape.
Primary local evidence for runtime_root as read-only Step 1 scope metadata and for preview-safe readiness boundaries.
Primary local evidence for typed Step 1 provenance, confidence, trust ceilings, and runtime_write_performed=false.
Primary local evidence for the preview-first Step 1 sequence and the static-versus-runtime boundary.
Primary local evidence for runtime package boundaries, required preview files, and non-goals around runtime claims.
Local research evidence for stable versus freshness-sensitive source classes, trust ceilings, and deck-neutral source modeling.
Local research evidence for documented preview surfaces and for keeping Step 1 aggressive but fail-closed.
Primary external reference for deckstring structure, versioning, format encoding, heroes, and DBF-id-based card identity.
Primary external reference for card-data fields such as id, dbfId, cardClass, type, and collectible scope.
Official Blizzard confirmation that public card-library and card-API surfaces exist.
Representative current meta source that should be treated as dated_meta_claim or guide_interpretation rather than stable identity proof.
Representative matchup-data source that must stay freshness-scoped and never become runtime proof by itself.
